resources.description: Diogo Almeida introduces Jev, the System One framing, RLCD, launch demonstrations, and the qualifications behind the reported performance gains. The starting point for this collection.

resources.title: AI: too good to be true, too bad to be useful

resources.title: Choice, Score, and Noul

resources.title: Confidence

resources.title: Jev 1.13 jaggedness

resources.title: TypeSafe A raises Series AI
resources.description: TypeSafe announces an $870 million Series A at a $7.5 billion valuation, led by Andreessen Horowitz with Sequoia and DCVC participating, and Martin Casado joining the board. Outlines plans for more machine-native models and enterprise infrastructure; this is a financing announcement, not a new Jev model release.

resources.title: How Jack & Jill Cut Candidate Screening Costs By 88% With Jev
resources.description: TypeSafe customer case study comparing Jev with Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite for initial candidate screening across 150 roles. Reports lower token cost and median completion time, with no statistically significant recall difference. Annual savings are projections; the outcome measures retention of hiring-manager selections rather than hiring fairness.
resources.date_note: The publisher page as retrieved by web search displays October 7, 2026. The current redesigned HTML omits the visible date; site build timestamps are not used as the publication date.

resources.title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
resources.description: Launch discussion with founder participation, questions about the API, architecture disclosure, calibration, and evaluation.

resources.title: Jev in 25 Lines of Python
resources.description: A deliberately minimal, explicitly satirical local implementation using option-token probabilities; the discussion probes what this does and does not reproduce.

resources.title: Ollaya – Ollama for open-source, Jev-style decision models
resources.description: Discussion of a local runtime for open decision models and compatibility with the TypeSafe interface.

resources.title: Jeff – Jev-compatible 0.8B decision models, trained at home, ~30 ms
resources.description: Release discussion for Jeff’s small decision models, local inference, and training approach.

resources.title: Kev: Tiny Jev-like family of decision models built on top of Qwen3.5
resources.description: Kev release discussion covering open weights, implementation choices, comparisons, and model size.

resources.title: OpenAI is well positioned to fast-follow Jev
resources.description: Debate about incumbent model providers, product differentiation, and Jev-style interfaces; market predictions are opinions.

resources.title: Show HN: Jev Plays Pokémon Red
resources.description: A Pokémon Red demonstration and discussion of the role of game state, legal actions, and the surrounding agent harness.

resources.title: Jeeves. Reasoning improves Jev-like decision models
resources.description: Jeeves release discussion about adding reasoning to Jev-style classifiers.

resources.title: Jev-Leftpad
resources.description: A humorous left-padding package powered by model decisions; useful as community history, not an infrastructure recommendation.

resources.title: Language models for text classification: From bag-of-words to Jev
resources.description: Discussion of Sebastian Raschka’s history of text classification and explanation of Jev-style decision interfaces.

resources.title: I turned Jev into a (lousy) chatbot
resources.description: An experiment generating text through repeated character choices, illustrating the limits of using Jev as a chatbot.

resources.title: Reverse-engineered Jev-like model
resources.description: Early independently built Jev-like option scorer; “reverse-engineered” in the thread title does not establish access to TypeSafe’s architecture.

resources.title: Show HN: JevBench, a reproducible benchmark for typed decision models
resources.description: Discussion of JevBench, its evaluation design, and cross-model comparisons.

resources.title: Jev Can't Be Calibrated
resources.description: Debate about distribution-dependent calibration and what a probability returned by Jev means.

resources.title: Jev introduces a new shape of LLM—System One, aka Decision Models
resources.description: Simon Willison explains the interface, experiments, open recreations, and the difficulty of inspecting a numeric decision.

resources.title: Language Models for Text Classification: From Bag-of-Words to Jev
resources.description: Sebastian Raschka places Jev in the history of classifiers, readout methods, and calibration; proposed internals are explicitly inferential.

resources.title: Building a Harness with Jev
resources.description: LangChain’s tutorial on integrating bounded decisions into an agent loop, including routing and evaluation.

resources.title: Building Prod with Jev and LangGraph
resources.description: LangChain’s worked document-review workflow combines Jev classifications, graph orchestration, and escalation.

resources.title: What is Jev? — Browserbase
resources.description: Browserbase explains how Stagehand can use Jev for bounded browser actions and fall back to an LLM.

resources.title: You could have built Jev
resources.description: Pete Sergeant explains option scoring and compares independent implementations; reproducing an interface does not prove model equivalence.

resources.title: Jev can’t be calibrated
resources.description: Alex Molas argues that calibration must be checked against the deployment distribution rather than assumed from a model-wide claim.

resources.title: Jev or a fine-tuned small model?
resources.description: Distil Labs reports a pipeline experiment comparing Jev and task-specific models on triage and invoice decisions. Results describe that vendor’s setup.

resources.title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
resources.description: Cloudflare introduces Jev-compatible multimodal decision models and describes its RL fine-tuning platform. Includes architecture and deployment details; benchmark comparisons are vendor-reported.

resources.title: Jev for Python engineers
resources.description: Vercel demonstrates typed Choice, Score, and Noul calls through its experimental Python evaluation API, including classification and AST generation. The examples also discuss failure cases.

resources.title: Jev is Poorly Calibrated
resources.description: Dylan Black tests option probabilities against known physical distributions and probes arithmetic failures. An author-run distribution-matching study, rather than a universal calibration verdict.

resources.title: The $40M Moat Lasted Two Weeks
resources.description: Abuiliazeed discusses Clef and Strands Decider as evidence of growing competition around Jev-style decision interfaces. An opinion essay on model commoditization and agent architecture; its market conclusions and benchmark comparisons are the author’s interpretation.

resources.title: System One models like Jev can train their own replacements
resources.description: Sean Goedecke proposes collecting inputs and decisions from a working Jev application to train a task-specific classifier. A distillation design argument, resurfaced in discussion, rather than a measured deployment study.

resources.title: Introducing d1: The most capable decision model, now with vision
resources.description: Liquid AI announces text-and-image typed decisions and demonstrations adapted from Jev ecosystem projects. Its application comparisons are vendor-run single trials. The announcement separates hosted availability from plans for future open-weight models.
resources.date_note: Date of the vision announcement. The article explicitly refers to an earlier experimental text release; this is not asserted to be the first availability of d1.

resources.title: Jev — AI Development Setup
resources.description: Steve Kinney explains where typed decisions fit into coding-agent routing, tool selection, context compaction, and verification. Distinguishes model-based risk signals from deterministic enforcement and recommends versioned, measured integrations.
resources.date_note: The original page exposes dateModified in its structured metadata; no first publication date is claimed.

resources.title: Jev Ultrafast: Pairing Browser Use with Jev
resources.description: Tien Nguyen Anh describes Browser Use for page perception and actions, with Jev choosing among available next steps. An architectural tutorial referencing jev-ultrafast; its speed and cost discussion is not an independent benchmark.

resources.title: Q: Is Jev useful for voice agents? A: Let's benchmark it
resources.description: Veris compares a Jev turn gate with silence-based detection on 100 simulated voice tasks, three runs each. Reported interruptions fall from 52% to 11%, while median replies slow from 2.1 to 4.6 seconds and task completion barely changes; the two conditions also use different Pipecat versions.

resources.title: Decide with Jev: Three Questions in One Request with the Laravel AI SDK
resources.description: Harris Raftopoulos demonstrates versioned Boolean, choice, and score questions in one request, a shared PHP service, answer decoding, and application-side dependencies between decisions. Includes the episode and example repository.

resources.title: Generate Jev Schemas from TypeScript Types
resources.description: Jeongho Nam shows how Typia generates question maps and answer decoders from TypeScript types and comments, using the direct Jev SDK or Vercel AI SDK. The MIT-licensed implementation includes a Boolean-to-Noul adapter; schema validation does not establish decision accuracy.
resources.date_note: The article displays September 30, 2026; its October 6 Hacker News submission is not the publication date.

resources.title: An Independent Evaluation of TypeSafe's Jev
resources.description: Vals evaluates twelve systems on 400 SEC-filing claim checks and a preregistered 396-question LegalBench slice. Jev matches several frontier models on claim verification but ranks last on this legal slice; its selective-automation test also exceeds the targeted error budget. Cost and latency findings are workload-specific.

resources.title: Is Jev the right model for your agents?
resources.description: Akhilesh Krishnan compares Jev, Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4-mini, and Gemini 3.5 Flash on two balanced 200-item support-escalation and model-routing datasets. Discusses latency, separate judge costs, and threshold sensitivity; the small samples and exploratory threshold adjustment limit generalization.
resources.date_note: First-party publication metadata predates the October 6 discussion submission.

resources.title: Jev plays chess
resources.description: Byren Cheema reports 470 games and 1,000 held-out puzzles, with every legal move supplied as an option. The experiment separates fast, legal outputs from weak chess play and investigates attraction to moves described as checks; code and recorded results are linked.

resources.title: Jev isn't a better judge than Claude
resources.description: DoubtBench author compares Jev and three Claude models on 7,455 HelpSteer2-derived judgments, including agreement with human uncertainty. Reports similar composite scores and weak tracking of annotator disagreement despite different cost and latency. Claude probabilities are generated in JSON, and reasoning effort and dataset scope limit the comparison.

resources.title: Do Jev Decision Models work for mine operations?
resources.description: Hivekit founder explains how Jev could interpret shift notes alongside deterministic scheduling calculations and safety constraints. Describes an application architecture and early integration direction, without a quantitative evaluation of mine operations.
resources.date_note: The first-party blog index dates this article 28.09.2026; a September 30 author repost corroborates earlier availability. October 7 aggregation is not its publication date.

resources.title: Build a Custom Jev Connector and Shared Pipelines in Maia
resources.description: First-party walkthrough of creating a TypeSafe connector, managing credentials through a secrets manager, and sharing batch, table, and answer-unpacking pipelines. Demonstrates a Snowflake-targeted integration with reusable examples; it is a vendor tutorial rather than an independent benchmark.

resources.title: What Is RSI-Jev? A Self-Improving Loop That Builds Jev-Style Decision Models
resources.description: Technical guide to RSI-Jev release history, adaptive-depth decision heads, serving, and evaluation caveats. Focuses on v6.0-VL while acknowledging v6.1-VL; performance figures come from the project, and the article explicitly says OrcaRouter does not host RSI-Jev.

resources.title: JEV-27B-VL: a decision model that learned to see without image training
resources.description: AutoTrust announces its independent multimodal decision model and explains reuse of a text-trained decision head with a vision-capable backbone. Reports a cover-image recommendation experiment on 200 users; these publisher-run findings do not establish general visual reliability.

resources.title: A lifejacket for scientists drowning in papers
resources.description: A. Sina Booeshaghi describes author.link and compares Jev with OpenAI Decisions for paper relevance using a 66-paper author-specific test and RELISH. Distinguishes relevance from scientific quality and cautions that a returned score is not a validated probability of usefulness.

resources.title: Classifying Emails with Jev and the OpenAI Decisions API
resources.description: Shrivu Shankar compares 40 model configurations on 1,985 non-public synthetic emails with 40% attacks. Contrasts calibration, recall at high precision, and attack-type classification; a fine-tuned Kev improves one metric while degrading another. The selected prevalence and private synthetic data limit generalization.

resources.title: Jev for Analytics: 5 Use Cases on Real Data
resources.description: Mehdi Ouazza demonstrates MotherDuck’s prompt_jev() SQL function on agent logs, Hacker News sentiment, sales calls, and job listings, with a consumer-complaints introduction. Shows context, fallback choices, and confidence-based review; these are vendor demonstrations rather than an independent benchmark.

resources.title: Investing in TypeSafe AI
resources.description: Andreessen Horowitz explains its investment thesis around Jev and decision models as software components. Offers the lead investor’s perspective on developer adoption and software economics; adoption, speed, and cost claims are investor statements rather than independent measurements.

resources.title: What we learned building 38 projects with Jev in 12 hours
resources.description: GC AI reports hackathon experiments in clause screening, streaming citation checks, alert triage, and a Slack pet. Explains narrow question design, context cleanup, confidence-based routing, and failures on arithmetic and broad judgments. The findings come from small internal experiments, not a general benchmark.

resources.title: Introducing Clef-omni, a faster Clef, and a cheaper Clef-flash
resources.description: Cloudflare introduces an independent Jev-compatible model for text, images, audio, and video. The announcement also describes faster Clef serving and a Clef-flash hosted price reduction with a shorter hosted context window; existing Clef and Flash weights are unchanged. Performance comparisons are vendor evaluations.

resources.title: If LLMs Can Decide Without Fine-Tuning, Do We Still Need Models Like Jev?
resources.description: Local experiments compare answer-logit scoring from general models with Jeff, Laya, and other decision implementations on small fixed tasks. TypeSafe Jev itself was not tested. Model size, quantization, prompts, and runtime differ, so the results do not isolate the effect of decision-model training.

resources.title: Jev and the Return of Fuzziness
resources.description: Reflects on Jev as a way to expose graded judgments inside deterministic software, relating decision interfaces to fuzzy reasoning and routing. This is a conceptual essay; its illustrative API examples are not a verified SDK reference.

resources.title: Using Jev in Domain Abuse Review: A Workflow Design
resources.description: ABTdomain describes a staged brand-protection prototype combining name classification, deterministic domain checks, and a narrowly framed use assessment. Tests use 100 Apple-containing names, including manual controls. Outputs support human review; the prototype is not a validated legal judgment system.
resources.date_note: Publisher displays October 9 publication and October 10 update. Publication date is retained; the October 10 HN submission is not the original date.

resources.title: How developers see Jev: praise, skepticism, and Chinese-language experiments
resources.description: Traditional Chinese overview of launch debates, calibration concerns, and task-specific tests, including the author’s website-navigation experience. The page is dated October 11 but explicitly bases its community evidence on September 27; historical attention figures are not current measurements.
resources.date_note: Visible date and datePublished identify October 11. The body gives September 27 as its source-check cutoff, and dateModified predates datePublished; the displayed publication date is not treated as a new experiment date.

resources.title: Using Jev to make your agents write the code and design the app the way you do
resources.description: Atul describes scoped, testable review rules inspired by Jev, with a CLI that turns code diffs and screenshots into per-rule judgments. Filed actually uses Perplexity’s decider in production, including for images. Examples include illustrative numbers, and tuning rule wording on a few cases can overfit.

resources.title: Using Jev With LangChain: Model Routing and Guardrails
resources.description: Dinesh Gopal demonstrates TypeSafeClassifier composition, model routing, and experimental tool-call screening with loan-intake examples. The blocking middleware does not request human approval, and only listed tools are classified. Examples illustrate integration patterns rather than measured safety or cost guarantees.

resources.title: Laya author’s prior-work discussion
resources.description: First-person account linking earlier sales-prediction and confidence-routing work. Architectural equivalence and priority claims are disputed and are not established by this thread.
resources.date_note: The dated September 17 prior-art entry links this exact Reddit thread. A separate Reddit trends archive records 2026-09-17 04:18 UTC; Reddit itself did not expose an absolute timestamp in this check. The day is inferred from these external records.

resources.title: Is Jev a new model class or a classifier?
resources.description: Community debate about novelty, zero-shot classification, and the difference between a useful product and a new architecture.
resources.date_note: An archival copy of the exact Reddit post is dated September 23; independent coverage also assigns that date. The original Reddit timestamp was unavailable, so this is an inferred posting date.

resources.description: Broad community directory of integrations, demos, and independent tests. Used for discovery; listed projects should be checked at their original sources.

resources.description: Community collection with projects, skills, demonstrations, and a curated social-post gallery.

resources.description: MIT community directory grouping Jev integrations, compatible models, clients, agent tools, and research. Useful for discovering upstream projects; its inclusion criteria, star counts, and capability descriptions are curator claims rather than independent verification.

resources.description: Official synchronous and asynchronous Python client for Jev.

resources.title: TypeSafe JavaScript / TypeScript SDK
resources.description: Official client with inferred answer types and typed question helpers.

resources.title: TypeSafe Agent Skills
resources.description: Official integration guidance for coding agents and skill-compatible tools.

resources.title: System One Adapter
resources.description: Official adapter that runs the decision interface over other LLM APIs for comparisons; it does not expose Jev weights.

resources.title: WorkflowEvals
resources.description: Source code for TypeSafe’s workflow evaluations. Its reference answers come from other models.

resources.title: TypeSafe n8n nodes
resources.description: Official repository for connecting the TypeSafe API to n8n workflows.

resources.title: Vercel AI Gateway
resources.description: Provider announcement and usage examples for accessing Jev through AI Gateway.

resources.title: Cloudflare Jev access
resources.description: Provider-maintained Jev model page and structured evaluation examples.
resources.date_note: The September 18 availability entry links the exact Cloudflare model page and explicitly calls this a documented-by date. It does not establish a go-live date for the current serving interface.

resources.description: Provider playground for turning a task into typed Jev questions.
resources.date_note: This exact Prompt to questions playground was inspected in the October 3 catalog and checked again on October 5. Searches found earlier OpenRouter Jev API announcements, but none dating this specific playground; the earlier API dates are not transferred to it.

resources.title: Netlify AI Gateway
resources.description: Provider documentation covering gateway configuration and TypeSafe integration.
resources.date_note: Netlify officially announced Jev availability in its AI Gateway on September 17, 2026. The date refers to the integration announcement, not the generic documentation page.

resources.title: Vercel AI SDK for Python: experimental Jev evaluation
resources.description: Apache-2.0 Python SDK with an experimental typed evaluation API for Jev through AI Gateway. Supports Choice, Score, and Noul questions; the date refers to the integration article, not repository creation.

resources.title: Liquid d1 with vision — hosted decision API
resources.description: Independent hosted alternative using Jev-style Choice, Score, and Noul requests. The October 5 announcement adds image inputs to Liquid’s own API; Vercel and OpenRouter support text only in that announcement. Public d1 weights were not located.
resources.date_note: Dates the vision feature announcement, not the earlier text preview or the creation of the playground.

resources.title: Microsoft-Decision-1
resources.description: Independent hosted Qwen3.5-9B-based decision-scoring model introduced by Microsoft. Vercel documents access through a TypeSafe-compatible API. Supports fixed-option probabilities, ratings, and rubric grading; published speed, calibration, and robustness results are vendor evaluations. No downloadable weights were located in the launch materials.

resources.title: SubQ Snap
resources.description: Subquadratic’s hosted public-preview decision model exposes a TypeSafe-compatible System One endpoint for Choice, Score, and Noul. Documents a 384K-token context and image input, with limited preview capacity. Comparisons against Jev, including chunked long-context baselines, are vendor-reported. No downloadable weights or training code are linked in the announcement.

resources.title: Langfuse System One-compatible evaluators
resources.description: Langfuse extends its TypeSafe evaluator connection with custom upstream URLs, including SubQ Snap and self-hosted Strands Decider. Stores typed answers, probabilities, and execution traces for online, batch, and experiment evaluations. Langfuse Cloud requires publicly reachable HTTPS endpoints for custom providers; local servers need self-hosted configuration.

resources.title: Jev Ultrafast
resources.description: Browser Use’s agent represents available browser actions as candidates and uses Jev to select operations and targets.

resources.title: Jev Browser
resources.description: Playwright navigation exposed as a library, CLI, and MCP server, with bounded action selection.

resources.title: Jev MCP — Python
resources.description: MCP server exposing classification, scoring, checking, matching, and screening through Jev.

resources.title: Jev MCP — Node
resources.description: MCP tools for evidence checks, ranking, candidate selection, extraction, and patch review.

resources.title: Jev-Mem
resources.description: Agent memory architecture using fast decisions for organization and retrieval, with a separate model for answer synthesis.

resources.title: Jev Form Fill
resources.description: MIT-licensed Chrome extension that uses Jev to propose exact source-text values for form fields. Users review proposals before applying them; readback and undo are provided, while form submission remains manual. Requires hosted API access.

resources.title: jev-map
resources.description: MIT-licensed Python CLI and MCP server mapping functions to tests through static analysis and optional Jev-scored links. Records the evidence behind each link; missing links do not establish that a test can safely be skipped.

resources.title: dotpals
resources.description: MIT-licensed local observer for coding-agent changes, commands, and test output. Optional Jev or local Laya checks interpret unclear test results; the cloud option sends a redacted output excerpt to TypeSafe. Its broader checks also use deterministic logic.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation, not the first release date of a model or integration.

resources.title: jev-mcp-router
resources.description: MIT-licensed MCP gateway using Jev yes/no decisions to shortlist servers and tools before an LLM sees their schemas. Includes a maintainer-run, 111-request evaluation over 649 tools; reported savings trade off against tool-selection coverage.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation, not the first release date of a model or integration.

resources.title: Jevline
resources.description: Experimental incident reconstruction from a confirmed malicious seed and exported telemetry. Jev judges which connected entities belong to the incident, producing a timeline and evidence table. Relatedness scores are not maliciousness verdicts, and results require analyst review; no repository license was declared in GitHub metadata.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation timestamp; not an independently verified first public release date.

resources.title: Orbs
resources.description: MIT-licensed multi-bot chat application with local Bun or Cloudflare hosting. Explicit mentions select bots; otherwise Jev scores who should reply. A local daemon executes turns through the separately installed Pi agent.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation; not an independently verified first public release date.

resources.title: jev-max
resources.description: Jev-powered browser agent that pierces shadow DOM and iframes into one indexed action table, with a vision fallback for canvas, uploads, drag-and-drop, multi-tab control, and an MCP server for any agent host.

resources.title: Jev Agent Control
resources.description: MIT OpenCode V2 server plugin that uses Jev to choose primary agents and reassess unfinished work at execution boundaries. Follows configured agent models, supports confidence thresholds and manual overrides, and reports testing against OpenCode 2.0.24.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Codex Route Advisor
resources.description: MIT planning skill that decomposes development work and recommends model, reasoning-effort, and tool allocation. Optional Jev assessment has a fallback when unavailable or uncertain. It produces a dispatch plan; the host coordinator retains execution and validation responsibility, and it does not switch the main chat model.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Competitor Monitor with Jev
resources.description: Apache-2.0 Mastra template that compares public competitor pages with stored snapshots, asks Jev to classify changes, and uses an LLM to explain source-linked evidence. Preserves before/after excerpts and review states; unchanged captures can skip classification.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: decisionkit
resources.description: MIT CLI, Claude Code plugin, and MCP server for typed decisions through Jev directly or via OpenRouter, OpenAI Decisions, or Claude. Preserves provider identity and errors. Claude returns self-reported probabilities; the included comparison uses 100 author-written tasks and does not establish a general accuracy ranking.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Jev Pilot
resources.description: Apache-2.0 experimental CLI proxy that asks Jev to recommend model capability and reasoning effort for Codex CLI and Claude Code. Supports allowed-model scopes and local usage reports. Long Codex sessions have had unresolved stream interruptions; task quality and subscription-quota savings remain unvalidated.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: skimmer
resources.description: MIT Go CLI that asks Jev which chunks of pages, local files, or list items help a stated goal. Retains source line references and keeps chunks when judging fails. Filtering can reduce downstream context, but the examples do not establish general answer-quality improvements.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Jev Harness — Apixly
resources.description: MIT Python runtime for Jev-selected tools and parameters drawn from fresh candidate sets. Separates observations, bounded execution, and independent completion checks, with browser and workspace examples. Historical live evidence uses small fixtures; the runtime is not a sandbox or an exactly-once execution service.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: DeciLabel
resources.description: MIT GitHub Action that uses Jev or other decision providers to add evidence-supported labels to issues and pull requests. Preserves existing labels, respects recorded human removals, and abstains on uncertain or malformed answers. Its Jev threshold evaluation is specific to one repository taxonomy.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Smart Find
resources.description: MIT Chrome extension that splits a page into passages, asks Jev which passages answer a question, and highlights matching source text. Sends page text to TypeSafe when a search is requested. Reported latency and answer coverage come from a small author-run test.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: PBI Orchestration with Jev
resources.description: MIT Claude Code skill that splits work into bounded items and routes them using deterministic facts plus Jev judgments of novelty, coupling, and ambiguity. Sends short task briefs and reports to Jev; verification commands decide completion. Includes capped rework loops and fallback routing, without a controlled end-to-end quality evaluation.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Jev Skill Router
resources.description: MIT OpenCode plugin using two gated Jev calls to select at most one skill, with abstention and whole-document budget checks. Larger skill catalogs first use BM25 retrieval. Its reported 96% top-one result is an offline retrieval baseline on 30 requests with synthetic distractors, not a live Jev selector accuracy measurement.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: JevReader
resources.description: Python MCP prototype combining local outlines, BM25 retrieval, and Jev judgments over code or document previews. Returns line-referenced chunks and skipped ranges; falls back to outlines or candidates when judging fails. Previews reach TypeSafe through a remote adapter. Public source is available, but no repository-wide license or controlled quality comparison was identified.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: jevcrawl
resources.description: Apache-2.0 crawler and MCP server using Jev to score links and passages, returning verbatim excerpts with source offsets. Reports small WebWalkerQA experiments with a shared downstream answering model; accuracy differences are less certain than cost differences. It does not execute page JavaScript, and typed scoring alone does not establish prompt-injection immunity.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: brojev
resources.description: Independent Go browser agent and Claude Code plugin using Chrome DevTools Protocol and Jev-selected operations and targets. Keeps a browser daemon and profiles across calls, validates actionability, and returns control on uncertainty or repeated failures. Text generation may use a helper model. Main code is MIT, with Apache-2.0 Playwright-derived portions.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Jev Phone
resources.description: MIT Python SDK that binds numbered screenshot candidates to device-tree coordinates for Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS taps. Despite its name, the documented default uses OpenAI Decisions through OpenRouter, not TypeSafe Jev. The caller supplies each target; planning and business assertions remain outside the SDK. Published millisecond timings distinguish local work from model round trips and full steps.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: DuckDB Jev
resources.description: DuckDB extension for Jev-backed predicates, classification, and scores over rows.

resources.title: pg-jev
resources.description: PostgreSQL extension for Jev-based row filtering, classification, and scoring. Version 0.2.1 adds local Jev-compatible servers without API keys and clarifies cache memory bounds. Public code uses the PostgreSQL license; hosted inference remains a separate service.

resources.title: jev — CLI and skill
resources.description: Community command-line wrapper supporting direct TypeSafe and OpenRouter backends.

resources.title: Jev Java
resources.description: Community Java client with typed questions and configurable retries.

resources.title: jev — Haskell
resources.description: Community Haskell client with composable typed questions and probability-preserving responses.

resources.title: Jev Doc Search
resources.description: VectifyAI uses Jev choices to navigate PageIndex document trees and select relevant PDF pages without an embedding index. Public Apache-2.0 code; hosted model access is a separate dependency.

resources.title: TypeSafeSharp
resources.description: Unofficial MIT-licensed .NET client for the TypeSafe System One API, with typed Jev answers, retries, dependency injection, and OpenTelemetry support. Targets netstandard2.0 and net10.0; not endorsed by TypeSafe AI.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation; not an independently verified first public release date.

resources.title: jev-bisect
resources.description: MIT Python library that uses Jev higher/lower/exactly decisions to search a bounded numeric grid. Exposes decision history, finite precision, and explicit exhaustion limits; numerical search remains dependent on the model making correct comparisons.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every feature.

resources.title: Jevector
resources.description: Builds criterion-based profile vectors with Jev or Clef, retrieves candidates through HNSW, and applies bilateral requirements. Includes BM25/BGE comparisons on only 52 synthetic profiles and eight queries; the results do not establish general retrieval superiority. Public code has no explicit license.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every feature.

resources.title: SystemOneClient — Elixir
resources.description: Apache-2.0 Elixir client for Jev, Clef, OpenRouter, and compatible self-hosted endpoints. Preserves full answer distributions and provides retry handling, telemetry, tagged errors, and a no-network test stub behind a shared interface.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: question-kit
resources.description: MIT TypeScript building blocks for Jev question design, classification, extraction, ordering, and service agents. Combines deterministic procedures with confidence-gated model readings and includes a pizza-shop demo. The API is alpha; reported internal evaluations are not public and live customer deployment is not established.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: LLM Context Optimizer
resources.description: MIT TypeScript SDK that selects explicitly supplied document context before native provider requests. Uses a local heuristic by default with an optional Jev scoring backend, protected documents, and budget checks. Initial source release; synthetic offline tests do not establish answer-quality preservation or net cost savings.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: jev — Rust decision CLI
resources.description: Rust CLI exposing structured typed questions across TypeSafe, compatible hosted services, and local providers, with OS-keychain credential storage. Code is dual MIT/Apache-2.0. Chat-logprob adapters have option and rubric limits; their entropy-based confidence should not be treated as validated task calibration.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: @amatelic/jev
resources.description: MIT TypeScript interface for local Choice, Noul, and Score inference, with embedded and HTTP transports, model caching, and schema validation. Documents Kev/Open-Jev model aliases and automatic downloads. The README supplies integration examples but no independent calibration or task-quality evaluation; model artifacts retain their upstream terms.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Laya
resources.description: Independent encoder-based decision models with English, multilingual, and workflow-specialist checkpoints; includes training and local serving.

resources.title: Kev
resources.description: Qwen-based family with released decision checkpoints, training code, evaluation suites, and TypeSafe-compatible serving.

resources.title: Bespoke Nimble
resources.description: Independent decision model with a contrastive data-curation recipe and public benchmark comparisons. Its authors state it was not distilled from Jev.

resources.title: Jeff — firelex
resources.description: Small decision models with local inference and domain adapters; distinct from other projects also called Jeff.

resources.title: Jeeves
resources.description: PostHog’s reasoning decision model, adding a diffusion drafter to a Qwen-based classifier; not a strictly one-pass decision model.

resources.title: Contrastive Language Models
resources.description: Contrastive state/action modeling with a TypeSafe-compatible API and an independently released 8B model.

resources.title: Vev
resources.description: Independent visual and textual decision models based on Qwen3.5, with 4B and 9B releases.

resources.title: WebJev
resources.description: Decision-model fine-tune specialized for browser actions; includes live-web data and evaluation harnesses.

resources.title: NanoJev
resources.description: Compact 0.6B model and training pipeline for parallel decisions in game environments; its scope is narrower than general hosted Jev.

resources.title: this-that-model-1.0
resources.description: A 2B typed-decision model with a research preprint. Reported speed and cost depend on its hardware and evaluation setup.

resources.title: Clef and Clef-flash
resources.description: Cloudflare releases independent multimodal decision models with Jev-compatible interfaces, using Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones respectively. Weights and decision-head inference code are available under Apache-2.0. An October 9 serving update lowers the hosted Flash price to $0.038/M input tokens and its context limit to 24k; existing weights are unchanged.

resources.title: Strands Decider 2B
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-2B-Base decision model with LoRA and a pointer readout for runtime-supplied Choice, Score, and Noul questions. Code and weights are Apache-2.0; training data retain their source licenses.

resources.title: GEV-26B-Decide
resources.description: AutoTrust decision model based on Gemma 4 26B-A4B, formerly named JEV-Gemma4-26B-A4B with unchanged weights. Adapter, head, and calibration files use Apache-2.0; the backbone retains Gemma terms.
resources.date_note: The model card has a New (3 October 2026) section documenting demonstrations with this checkpoint. It says the weights were previously published as JEV-Gemma4-26B-A4B, so this bounds availability of the named artifact and does not date the first weight release.

resources.title: Gutsy
resources.description: Small Qwen3.5-0.8B decision model exposing a Jev-style API through llama.cpp, with CPU-oriented GGUF quantizations. The repository and released model weights use Apache-2.0; upstream training datasets have separate terms.

resources.title: Tasksource-JEV-Nano v1
resources.description: Apache-2.0 weights for a compact ModernBERT/LateOn-based decision model using late interaction. The former v0 URL resolves to this v1 repository. Decision metadata and weight files are public, but the current card largely reproduces the base retrieval model documentation rather than a dedicated v1 evaluation.
resources.date_note: The former v0 API resolves to the v1 repository with the same createdAt timestamp. This preserves repository creation evidence; neither the rename date nor the first public release date of v1 weights is established.

resources.title: Jevling-E2B-v1
resources.description: Gemma 4 E2B-based typed decision fine-tune emphasizing Traditional Chinese kiosk transcripts, with Safetensors and GGUF weights. The checkpoint and base model declare Apache-2.0; its custom runtime is a separate artifact.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp from the original API response retrieved on 2026-10-05. Repository creation is not asserted to be the first public release of the weights or dataset.

resources.title: jiwo 0.8B and 4B
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-based decision models with a Jev-compatible server and typed probability readouts. Model weights are Apache-2.0 and serving code is MIT. Reported Decision Index results are author submissions, not independently verified leaderboard results.
resources.date_note: Dates the earliest of the two checked model repositories, jiwo-0.8b. The jiwo-4b repository was created 2026-10-05T07:37:22.000Z. Neither timestamp establishes when its weights first became public.

resources.title: Archai JEV Nesso 4B Ita
resources.description: Italian Jev-style decision model adapted from Nesso 4B, targeting single-token options for moderation, sentiment, and inference tasks. Public files include a QLoRA adapter and Q8 GGUF; the model card declares Apache-2.0. Accuracy and calibration figures are author-reported, not independent verification.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; it does not establish when model weights first became public.

resources.title: JEVnovel 2.5 — Chinese prose revision detectors
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-based 0.8B and 4B decision models that locate formulaic spans in Chinese web fiction using prefix and clause heads, distilled from a 27B teacher. Both repositories publish weights and custom inference code under Apache-2.0. They assess stylistic impressions, not factual correctness; other writing domains are unvalidated.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; it does not establish when model weights first became public.

resources.title: Jev Recovery Router
resources.description: Independent Jev-inspired research bundle combining a Qwen3-1.7B adapter, decision head, calibrated retrieval, and a separate cost-conditioned recovery actor. Public Apache-2.0 code and adapter/head/actor weights support commit, expand, or handoff decisions. Requires upstream base weights and custom inference; BANKING77 transfer remains a disclosed failure case.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; it does not establish when model weights first became public.

resources.title: RSI-Jev v6.1-VL
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-4B-based text-and-image decision model with adaptive exits at layers 16, 20, and 32, produced by averaging two fine-tunes. MIT code and declared Apache-2.0 weights are public. The card discloses restricted training-data terms and worse calibration than v6.0-VL despite author-reported accuracy gains.

resources.title: InnerJev-4B-Full
resources.description: Apache-2.0 complete BF16 weights with Apache-2.0 training and inference code. Distills reasoning-derived option distributions into a text-only decision readout with thinking disabled. The released full-rank adaptation covers selected language layers; reported BF16 scores are not quantized-inference results.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation, not the release date of every contained artifact.

resources.title: AutoTrust JEV-27B-VL
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.8-27B-based model combining text-and-image typed decisions with a separate generative path. Apache-2.0 weights, decision adapter, and serving code are public. The card documents custom vLLM serving constraints and limited visual calibration evidence; it is not TypeSafe Jev.

resources.title: Together Tev1-4B-experimental
resources.description: Jev-inspired Qwen3.5-4B supervised fine-tune that generates one option letter, with a public MIT training recipe and downloadable weights. The model card says the fine-tuned weight license is still being finalized; development-set results and token logprobs are not independent accuracy or calibration guarantees.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation; not an independently verified first public release date.

resources.title: RSI-Jev v6.1-VL 27B
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.8-27B-based text-and-image decision model with exits at layers 48, 56, and 64. Self-contained Apache-2.0 weights and MIT serving code are public. The card discloses restricted training-data terms, selection using repeated public-benchmark evaluations, and worse calibration than its 4B counterpart.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp, not a verified first public release date for the weights or dataset.

resources.title: Laya Darija 25-domain classifier
resources.description: Independent Laya multilingual fine-tune for Moroccan Darija, Arabizi, and French-mixed text. Public weights select one of 25 fixed topic labels without an unknown option. The author reports evaluation on noisy synthetic labels and weaker Arabizi performance. No explicit license for this fine-tune was located.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp, not a verified first public release date for the weights or dataset.

resources.title: Dex 1B
resources.description: Independent Jev-compatible model combining an Ettin-1B encoder with a Laya-style typed decision head. Apache-2.0 code and weights are public. Author-run comparisons report gains over stock Laya on some tasks, with gaps to Jev, limited context and option coverage, and shared training/benchmark sources.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: MATILDA JEV v1.5
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.8-27B-based text decision model with a 255-option readout and merged weights. Apache-2.0 weights and custom runtime are public. Its Decision Index results are diagnostic: the card discloses benchmark-related training material and checkpoint selection using experimental scores; vision was not validated.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Haidass1.5-143M-Jev
resources.description: Research decision model using a frozen Haidass backbone, LoRA, and a Kev-style option pointer head. Publishes Apache-2.0 adapters, head, tokenizer, and experiment code; the backbone is a separate download. Reports development-set metrics only, with a single seed and substantial option-order sensitivity.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Clef-omni
resources.description: Cloudflare’s independent Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-based model adds typed decisions over text, images, audio, and video. Apache-2.0 weights, a joint decision head, and custom inference code are public. Uses the comprehension backbone; the card lists SGLang support as forthcoming.

resources.title: Jev-Darija Telecom Model
resources.description: Laya-based classifier for Moroccan Darija telecom messages across Arabic script, Arabizi, and French mixtures. Predicts category, intent, product, urgency, and human escalation using two-stage questions. Apache-2.0 weights and prediction code are public; reported evaluation uses a synthetic test set without native-speaker review.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: JEVnovel 3 — fragment-level Chinese prose revision
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-0.8B model with fragment-level quality and information-density heads to suggest deleting or rewriting Chinese prose. Apache-2.0 BF16 weights and custom inference code are public. Teacher-derived supervision and author-run human-preference evaluations support this narrow revision task, not general Jev compatibility.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: AutoTrust JEV-35B
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-35B-A3B decision model with merged typed readout, public Apache-2.0 weights, and serving code. Supports text and zero-shot image decisions. Author-run Decision Index results exclude private tests, and vision scores use a reconstructed suite; sequential game performance is weaker than the prior JEV-27B-VL.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: PhysicalEye-Decide-35B
resources.description: Independent Darwin/Qwen3.5-based vision model using Jev-style Choice, Noul, and Score interfaces. Publishes Apache-2.0 backbone weights, decision readout, and inference code. Small egg-inspection and science-diagram evaluations are author-reported; temperature scaling alone does not establish calibration across deployment tasks.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: jev-vision-27b
resources.description: Apache-2.0 LoRA adapter for Qwen3.8-27B trained on text and image decision tasks, with merge and serving code. Uses option-label logits and rejects questions exceeding 62 options. The base weights are separate; reported vision results use the author’s reconstruction of public benchmarks rather than the official board.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Workmagic Jev Decision
resources.description: Qwen3-4B model distilled with AnyJev for Slack customer-churn decisions. Apache-2.0 weights are public and inference uses the external AnyJev runtime. Training uses teacher-generated answers without human labels; the card does not provide an independent held-out evaluation.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Archai Jev Zagreus 0.4B Italian
resources.description: Italian decision-model experiment with merged weights, LoRA adapters, and a GGUF conversion. Uses Decision Index-style option scoring. Version 2 reports in-distribution gains but no positive transfer to the tested unseen task groups. Downloadable artifacts are public; no explicit model license was found in the card or file listing.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Jev-class 9B SFT
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-9B-Base decision model trained with Mapika decider’s supervised recipe. Apache-2.0 weights and experiment code are public. Reports regression tests and 231 public JevBench items, with weaknesses on long option lists, JSON-heavy states, and some games. The code also documents LoRA and reinforcement-learning follow-ups; these do not establish broad superiority.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Social Jev 0.6B v1
resources.description: Qwen3-0.6B classifier using a custom layout and the pretrained language-model head. Public weights and custom inference code are provided without an explicit model license. Trained for 100 optimizer steps on generated tasks; the reported 93.45% selects among validation checkpoints, excludes overlong examples, and is not a held-out test score.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: On-Fly-Jev v2
resources.description: Experimental 96M spiking-network decision model with connectome-inspired components and a memory cache. Apache-2.0 weights and Python code are public. The author reports 41 correct answers on 100 fresh questions and weaker typed-decision accuracy than v1 despite further training; novelty of the architecture does not establish general Jev-equivalent capability.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Jev-chess 1 small — 6.5M
resources.description: Independent chess policy network inspired by Jev’s typed-choice interface, returning probabilities over legal moves without tree search. Publishes CC0-1.0 weights and UCI inference code. The card reports Stockfish-labeled training, held-out move accuracy, calibration, and a 200-game rating estimate; these are author measurements, not TypeSafe weights or independent replication.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Workmagic Jev Churn — Qwen3-8B v1
resources.description: Apache-2.0 Qwen3-8B checkpoint self-distilled with AnyJev for Slack customer-churn decisions, distinct from the earlier 4B release. Publishes merged weights for single-forward readout. Training uses teacher answers without human labels; the inspected card does not report a held-out evaluation.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Barcenas Jev 0.8B
resources.description: Mexican-Spanish contract-triage model based on Qwen3.5-0.8B, with public Apache-2.0 backbone weights, joint head, and custom model code. Predicts contract type, lawyer referral, risk, and urgency. Reported results use 100 synthetic test records; per-question accuracy differs from all-fields-correct record accuracy and does not establish real-contract legal reliability.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Archai Jev Qwen 1.5B
resources.description: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct fine-tune using option-key log-probabilities with Decision Index-compatible prompts. Publishes merged weights, LoRA, and GGUF, but no explicit model license was identified. Version 2 compares against the base on unseen tasks: near-family transfer is small and far-family transfer is flat, with regressions on some tasks.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Chinese-Jev
resources.description: Chinese decision-model training, calibration, and evaluation code. The project lists trained Chinese-Jev weights as planned, so this entry is not a downloadable-weight release.

resources.title: jev-270m
resources.description: Notebooks and training scripts studying a Jev-inspired decision interface on Gemma 3 270M. Compares stock token readouts, trained pointer heads, and LoRA. Code is Apache-2.0; Gemma weights and derived checkpoints retain Gemma terms.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation, not the first release date of a model or integration.

resources.title: Ollaya
resources.description: Local runtime for pulling and serving multiple decision-model families behind a TypeSafe-compatible API. Independent of Ollama and TypeSafe.

resources.title: AnyJev
resources.description: Nokia Applied Research’s library for typed readouts from open LLMs, including option-bias correction and calibration modes.

resources.title: SemIf-OpenJev
resources.description: Open-model option scoring and semantic conditionals; formerly named OpenJev and SemIf. This is an independent implementation.

resources.title: OpenJev SGLang
resources.description: Prefill-only decision serving over open models using SGLang.

resources.title: OpenJev — DiffusionGemma
resources.description: Independent TypeSafe-compatible server reading typed decisions from DiffusionGemma, with NVIDIA and Apple silicon paths.

resources.title: open-jev — daseinlabs
resources.description: Local Gemma option scorer using shared context and candidate sequence likelihoods.

resources.title: Jevlike
resources.description: Independent model and training starter that scores a changing set of candidate options in one pass.

resources.title: LibLayaX
resources.description: MIT-licensed shared library and C API built on laya.cpp for embedding Laya decisions inside an application without a separate server. Targets desktop and server platforms; model weights are downloaded separately from the Laya publisher.

resources.title: Browser Laya
resources.description: MIT-licensed browser library and playground for English Laya inference through ONNX Runtime Web, with WebGPU and WebAssembly paths. The linked Apache-2.0 ONNX weights are public; the default bundle is about 900 MB. The documented int8 export uses WebAssembly because of WebGPU correctness limitations.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation timestamp; not an independently verified first public release date.

resources.title: Bud Decision Studio
resources.description: Desktop interface and local server for independent Jev-style models, with model downloads, typed questions, evaluation, versioned templates, and LoRA training. Source is public, but no explicit project license was located; model licenses are separate. Performance and hardware support are author-reported.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every feature.

resources.title: iKev
resources.description: Swift/MLX port of Kev decision models with checkpoint conversion, parity checks, a message router, and a dungeon example. The linked checkpoint card declares MIT, while the Swift repository has no explicit license. Mac results are reported; iPhone latency and memory measurements remain pending.
resources.status: Public code; code license not stated
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every feature.

resources.title: JEV-9B with vision — Core ML
resources.description: Core ML conversion of AutoTrust’s independent JEV-9B, with merged decision adapters, an 8-bit decoder, and a vision tower for Apple silicon GPUs. Apache-2.0 artifacts and Swift runtime are available. Conversion parity was checked on only 36 decisions from 12 game frames; this does not validate general calibration.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: Laya MLX Jev Endpoint
resources.description: MIT FastAPI wrapper around laya-mlx on Apple silicon, exposing a System One-style endpoint for Choice, Score, and Noul requests. Supports structured states and a model catalog. It serves the independent Laya model; matching request shapes do not establish equivalent Jev behavior.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Granite–Jev sampling and selective verification
resources.description: MIT inference runner that generates greedy and sampled answers with unchanged Granite 4.0-1B weights, then optionally asks hosted Jev to select between disagreements. Publishes code, not newly trained weights. Both generations incur work, and exploratory results do not establish superiority at equal compute or cost. The card-linked paper and larger code repositories were unavailable when checked.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp; not asserted to be the first public release of weights or data.

resources.title: nano_jev
resources.description: Zero-dependency Python service implementing a deterministic keyword-and-heuristic screening layer compatible with jev-arena request shapes. Provides Chinese/English label vocabularies and an OpenAI-style adapter. It runs no neural model and is explicitly limited on sarcasm, implicit meaning, and long text. Public source is available; no repository-wide license was identified.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: laya-java
resources.description: Apache-2.0 Java port of Laya with a standalone server, Spring Boot starter, Gradle integration, and Jev-compatible requests. Downloads separate Laya checkpoints; supports optional Apple Accelerate. Reference-fixture agreement does not establish general task accuracy. Image input and several upstream prediction helpers are unsupported.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: FuZev
resources.description: Apache-2.0 serving components sharing a frozen language-model backbone between generation and Jev-compatible decisions. Publishes a separate 2.9M-parameter Apache-2.0 head for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Quality results use pre-release builds; full-context quality is unmeasured, vision remains experimental, and probability repeatability varies across engines and cache states.
resources.date_note: GitHub repository creation date; not asserted to be the first public release of every included artifact.

resources.title: Transformers decision pipeline proposal
resources.description: Open pull request adding Jev-like decision-model processing, readout heads, pipeline support, and System One serving changes to Transformers. A linked Apache-2.0 JEV-9B adapter/head package supplies converted decision files; the backbone remains separate. The pull request is unmerged as checked, so the proposal is not a released Transformers capability.
resources.date_note: Pull request creation timestamp; not a merge or package release date.

resources.title: JevBench
resources.description: Independent multi-model benchmark with versioned scoring and results. Only aggregate results are published.

resources.title: Jevals
resources.description: Public benchmark suites and per-decision results for hosted Jev and comparator models.

resources.title: Janus
resources.description: Calibration and cascade experiments using Jev and a larger fallback model on labeled classification tasks.

resources.title: jev-certify
resources.description: Conformal routing and auditing toolkit with a CLINC150 study; its guarantees depend on calibration and deployment assumptions.

resources.title: Jev benchmarking — AppliedMachineLearning-Lab
resources.description: Code accompanying the 37-dataset Jev evaluation; keep model versions and request templates fixed when reproducing it.

resources.title: RLCDAlignBench
resources.description: Benchmark of typed decisions for detecting alignment failures, with code and data linked from its paper.

resources.title: JevOut
resources.description: Research code for testing whether natural-looking context changes can redirect a decision model.

resources.title: DoubtBench
resources.description: Evaluates Jev and other decision models against human disagreement using typed questions derived from HelpSteer2. Reports accuracy, calibration, and distribution agreement. Code is MIT; derived data are CC BY 4.0. Results are maintainer-run.

resources.title: Tasksource typed decisions
resources.description: Recasts public task datasets into Choice, Score, and Noul supervision, including soft targets and grouped questions. Offers a smaller default mix and a full training set. Licenses remain source-dependent, with per-row provenance and usage labels.
resources.date_note: Hugging Face repository creation timestamp from the original API response retrieved on 2026-10-05. Repository creation is not asserted to be the first public release of the weights or dataset.

resources.title: Korean JEV Benchmark
resources.description: Publishes 25,418 Korean finite-choice items and an October 4 comparison of hosted Jev with local model configurations.
